feedback: No race telemetry exists yet, so this feedback rests on the contract and the iteration 0 design, not on any measured run. Integration points to watch: (1) H1 depends on the 12 mm footprint giving a clean reading gradient across the 25 mm tape. Use the first race's line_loss_events and steering_oscillation to check this. If line_loss_events is above zero on the oval or S-bend, the array is not reaching the tape at moderate offsets. (2) H2 depends on max_error staying below 0.06 m on tight bends. The controller will be tuned to keep max_error low, so if max_error still approaches 0.06 m, the limit is geometric and body_width or wheel_track need to change, not the gains. (3) H3 depends on completion_time. If the robot is slower than about 2.5 s, check whether wheel slip or low torque is the cause before changing the controller. The lookahead at y = 0.06 m adds phase lag, so if steering_oscillation is high, reduce kp before increasing kd. Decide the next geometry from what the race shows: if max_error is near 0.06 m with no line loss, widen body_width; if line loss occurs at offsets, widen the sensor span; if the robot is too slow to finish, lower mass or raise wheel_radius.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events is above zero on the oval or S-bend, widen the sensor span to x = +/-0.03 m (keeping the 10 mm pitch or adding a sensor) before changing the footprint. This follows the stated line-loss rule and the 25 mm tape width.

If max_error approaches 0.06 m on the tightest bend, increase body_width to 0.14 m (raising the off-track limit to about 0.065 m) or try a 0.14 m wheel_track for more turn authority. Test against the next race's max_error.
If completion_time exceeds 2.5 s, test mass 0.6 kg with wheel_radius 0.035 m, to reduce inertia and raise top speed without changing the track width, and compare completion_time against the baseline.
